thread:
maria: quick async standup — SDK / quickstart check-in

what I did: pushed v0.3.2 of the js-sdk quickstart, fixed readme examples and CI step that was failing on node 18. updated sampleapp to use the new streaming api options.

blockers: sampleapp flakes on mac M1 during pip install for the python example container. hitting brew/OpenSSL compile errors in CI image. can't repro locally on linux.

today: triage M1 install, add workaround to docs, and ping infra for a macos-latest runner or new base image. also review kevin's PR on streaming docs.

kevin: saw the PR, gave inline comments on the streaming section — mostly wording + example for function calling. I can take the docs edits after you push changes for the M1 note.

aj: for the M1 thing — I hit that before. quick workaround is to set env before build: 

```bash
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
pip install <package>
```

but that's a bad DX to put in the quickstart. better: create a prebuilt wheel and host it in the sampleapp CI job (or use cibuildwheel).

maria: yup. thinking two-pronged: 1) add an M1 troubleshooting blurb to quickstart (short, with link to more detail), 2) update CI to build wheels and cache them for the python sample container.

sam: I can help add cibuildwheel job. small Q: do we want to publish wheels to GH Packages or just cache artifacts in CI? less ops if GH Packages but requires org permissions.

lina: GH Packages SGTM, we already do that for some infra libs. I can request the repo scope.

kevin: for the docs example that uses streaming + function-calls, I think we should include a minimal Typescript snippet and also a curl fallback for people who can't run the SDK immediately. example: 

```ts
// TS streaming snippet (pseudo)
const stream = client.stream({ model: 'rw-llm-stream' });
stream.on('data', (chunk) => console.log(chunk.text));
stream.on('end', () => console.log('done'));
```

and curl fallback: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw-llm-stream","prompt":"hi"}'
```

maria: good call. keep curl example minimal and call out "no streaming" behavior. I'll add both.

deploy-bot: CI job "python-sampleapp-build" failed on macos-latest — exit code 2 — logs uploaded: https://ci.internal/reports/1812500000/python-sampleapp

aj: thanks deploy-bot link. looking at logs now, it's the native deps for tokenizers. suggests we should pin the tokenizer package to a prebuilt wheel where possible.

maria: plan for next 48h:
- add M1 troubleshooting blurb to quickstart (maria)
- open PR to add cibuildwheel GH action + publish to GH Packages (sam + lina)
- kevin to land streaming doc wording + curl fallback
- aj to add CI tweak to prefer wheel over source install

anyone blocking me on reviews?

kevin: I can take a first pass on the streaming doc review today.

sam: I'll start the cibuildwheel job, ping if you want me to mirror package to s3 instead of GH Packages.

lina: will request repo package permissions now, ETA a few hours.

maria: thanks — I'll carve out time this afternoon to update the quickstart and sampleapp README. ping here if you need any example snippets.

kevin: small nit — in sampleapp README the `REDWOOD_API_KEY` variable name is inconsistent with our env docs. prefer `REDWOOD_KEY`. please standardize.

maria: noted. will standardize to REDWOOD_KEY across samples.

sam: tagging this thread in the PRs so tracking is easier: PR #842 (sam) for wheels, PR #843 (kevin) for docs, PR #844 (maria) for quickstart text.

aj: thanks. no more from me — will post back when CI tweak merged. :thumbsup:

maria: closing the loop — will update last_message_ts when PRs land. thanks team!
